killed.title: CanopyBid Pro — Cross-Platform Browser & iPad 2D Horticulture CAD, Regional Plant Palettes & Live Takeoff Proposal Studio
killed.stage: Deep Dive — Rude Q&A + Dalio Panel

plausible.justification: 100,000 order of magnitude (clearly above the 31.6k log10 midpoint vs. 10k, clearly below 1M after behavioral filtering). Triangulated firm bases across target geographies: US Landscape Design = 48,649 businesses (IBISWorld 2026) and US Landscaping Services NAICS 561730 = ~115k-118k employer firms + ~538k nonemployers (US Census; ~75-85% residential and ~62-65% offering design-build/install per NALP/Lawn & Landscape surveys), plus UK ~24,700 landscaping firms (IBISWorld; SGD ~1.6k-2k designers), Canada ~20k-25k, Australia ~15k-20k, and Europe ~268k-300k landscaping businesses (IBISWorld/ELCA). Applying a strict 10-15% behavioral filter for firms drafting 10-40+ scaled 2D residential planting plans and itemized $5k-$75k bids/yr yields ~25k-45k US + ~8k-15k CA/UK/AU + ~25k-40k Western Europe = ~58k-100k qualified firms. Caveat: reaching 100k strictly requires cross-OS (Windows+Mac+iPad) and international regional botanical databases/localization; English-only US/CA/UK/AU sits near ~35k-60k.

self_aware.justification: 0.5 (industry standard practice). Dedicated landscape planting-plan and takeoff software is an established, actively budgeted category: PRO Landscape reports tens of thousands of landscape professional users, DynaScape is taught in 100+ North American schools and used by thousands of pros, and r/LandscapeArchitecture, r/landscaping, APLD, and SGD forums show continuous active shopping and complaints over Windows-only locks, steep CAD learning curves, and broken sketch-to-plant-list-to-spreadsheet workflows. Not 1.0 because many micro contractors still hand-sketch or prioritize 3D hardscape visualization over scaled 2D horticultural CAD.

lucrative.justification: $1,000/yr order of magnitude (above the $316/yr log10 midpoint vs. $100). Sticker price is $828/yr Solo Pro / $1,548/yr 3-seat Studio, directly supported by demonstrated mainstream annual allocation across live competitors serving 1-5 person residential design-build and pro design firms: PRO Landscape+ ($900/yr), VizTerra ($997/yr), ArcSite Takeoff/Estimate ($1,188-$1,548/yr), Vectorworks Landmark ($1,530/yr), and DynaScape Creator+Color ($1,629/yr) / Design+Color ($1,999/yr). Even the fragmented manual duct-tape stack (Morpholio Trace + PlantMaster + Office/Excel) runs ~$350-$400/yr. Caveat: solo non-build garden designers in UK/AU/US often anchor at $100-$350/yr (Shoot ~$300/yr, iScape $300/yr, Sow Pro+ $99.99/yr, gCADPlus $95 one-time), creating downward price pressure outside the design-build contractor core.

liquid.justification: 0.1 (annual/seasonal decision window). While standalone per-project files avoid multi-year ERP/payment-rail migration paralysis (not 0.01), residential landscape CAD adoption is tightly gated by northern-climate seasonality (March-October peak season leaves only a Nov-Feb winter off-season window to retrain and rebuild templates/nursery price catalogs — explicitly reflected in Vectorworks' 6-8 week winter DynaScape migration guides) plus annual prepayment cycles across DynaScape, Vectorworks, PRO Landscape+, and VizTerra. Cannot claim 1.0 impulse switching during spring/summer install rush.

eager_identity.justification: 0.5 (indifferent, no structural red flags). Solo residential designers and 1-5 person landscape contractors routinely buy software via credit card from small indie and boutique makers (gCADPlus, PlantMaster, Sow, Morpholio, Artifact Interactive, Drafix/PRO Landscape) with zero SOC 2, HIPAA, IRS, or institutional E&O/professional-stamp barriers (non-stamped residential planting layouts where buyer owns 100% of site plans and local nursery price sheets). An unvetted founder lacks brand pull (not 1.0) and must prove botanical data accuracy via reputable regional plant sources and clean PDF/CSV/DXF export escape hatches, but faces no structural buying bar (not 0.1).

eager_comparative.justification: 0.5 (ConvertKit-calibrated: clear sub-segment buys for this unified wedge alone, though heavily contested across the broader 100k pool — believability capped at 0.4 pending buyer WTP tests). Live primary-doc audit confirms no single rival cleanly combines browser + native iPad Apple Pencil scaled 2D Arch-D planting CAD + regional botanical DB + mature-canopy checks + auto-synced visual homeowner plant photo boards + live polygon cubic-mulch/edging/labor takeoff bid PDFs: DynaScape Creator+Color costs $1,629/yr (2x price, clunky mouse-only CAD, no iPad Pencil or visual photo boards); Vectorworks Landmark costs $1,530/yr (desktop-only BIM overkill); ArcSite ($1,188-$1,548/yr) and Rayon ($252-$456/yr) lack native horticultural plant DBs and photo boards; Morpholio Trace + PlantMaster + Excel (~$300/yr) breaks sync on every plant swap; Sow Pro+ ($99.99/yr) is satellite/AI photo-first without precision Arch-D 2D CAD or polygon mulch/edging takeoffs. CRITICAL DISQUALIFIER AUDIT (DP26): Pitch omitted PRO Landscape+ ($900/yr, which DOES include an iPad Companion CAD/proposal app + 18k plants + 2D + 3D, though anchored to dated Windows desktop), Realtime Landscaping Architect ($599 one-time, Windows-only 2D+3D+8k plants+takeoff), gCADPlus ($95 one-time, Windows-only 2D CAD+schedules), and UK's Shoot Gardening (~$300/yr, 35k UK/EU plants+2D). This creates a genuine 0.5 wedge for Mac/iPad residential planting designers and modern 1-5 person softscape design-build estimators, but severe risk on Windows and among 3D-expecting $25k-$75k hardscape-heavy contractors.

enduring.justification: 0.5 (recurring revenue from a recurring problem). Residential designers and design-build contractors draft 10-40+ planting plans and bids every year; incumbents (DynaScape, Vectorworks, PRO Landscape+, PlantMaster, ArcSite) sustain annual recurring subscription businesses on this exact workflow, reinforced by saved local nursery price catalogs, favorite plant palettes, and title-block templates. Capped at 0.5 (not 1.0) due to seasonal winter pause/cancellation risk on monthly plans ($89/mo), lack of downstream CRM/payments lock-in by deliberate trade-off, and multi-year competitive risk from Sow Pro+ moving upmarket or DynaScape modernizing for iPad.

scenario_a.band: VIABLE INDIE (>= 1.0 — can sustain an indie company)

plausible.justification: 10,000 order of magnitude (10x reduction from 100,000 after stripping DP14/DP21 TAM padding). The original 100,000 claim required (1) 25k-40k non-English Western European firms unreachable without German/French/Dutch localization, metric/EU nursery standards, and licensed European botanical IP (already served by DATAflor and Shoot Gardening), plus (2) Windows-content contractors (served by $900/yr PRO Landscape+ and $599 one-time Realtime), $25k-$75k hardscape-bundling contractors who require 3D/photo renders and CRM/job-costing suites (LMN, SingleOps, ArcSite Estimate), and low-WTP ($100-$350/yr) solo designers. Removing non-buyers and unreachable geographies cuts genuine behavioral TAM decisively below the 31,622 log10 midpoint into the 10,000 bucket.

self_aware.justification: 0.5 (established, actively budgeted software category). High incumbent density across desktop, browser, and iPad (PRO Landscape, DynaScape, Vectorworks, ArcSite, Sow Pro+, PlantMaster, Shoot Gardening, gCADPlus) proves buyers actively search and pay for landscape design and takeoff software — even as that same saturation eliminates our comparative wedge.

lucrative.justification: $1,000/yr order of magnitude ONLY when anchored to 1-5 person residential design-build contractors (PRO Landscape+ $900/yr, VizTerra $997/yr, ArcSite $1,188-$1,548/yr, Vectorworks $1,530/yr, DynaScape $1,629-$1,999/yr) — the exact segment disqualified by CanopyBid Pro's 2D-softscape-only CSV trade-offs (pinning Eager-Comparative at 0.1). If instead focused on the only Mac/iPad solo garden designers who might tolerate 2D-only softscape output, market anchors (Morpholio $25-$50/yr, Sow Pro+ $99.99/yr, PlantMaster $250/yr, Shoot ~£240/yr, gCADPlus $95 one-time, PRO Landscape Contractor $399.99/yr) compress Lucrative 10x to $100/yr (collapsing total score from 0.02 to 0.002).

liquid.justification: 0.1 (annual/seasonal switching freeze). Peak residential install season (March-October) confines CAD migration and catalog/template retraining to a ~12-week Nov-Feb winter window, reinforced by annual incumbent subscriptions. Any 6-week solo engineering slip forfeits an entire year of customer acquisition.

eager_identity.justification: 0.5 on narrow procurement mechanics only (credit-card self-serve buying from boutique software vendors with zero SOC 2/HIPAA/stamp barriers), WITH an explicit domain-trust penalty: an unvetted solo developer holds zero APLD/ASLA/SGD horticultural authority or licensed RHS/Monrovia botanical data, triggering active skepticism among professional garden designers over cultivar taxonomy, hardiness zones, and mature-canopy accuracy. Stripping curated botanical-publisher claims to preserve 0.5 procurement parity further seals Eager-Comparative at 0.1.

eager_comparative.justification: 0.1 (crowded floor-and-ceiling sandwich — objectively 'Less for More' across every verified rival). Live pricing and feature checks demolish the claimed cross-platform/iPad gap: PRO Landscape Contractor ALREADY delivers standalone iPad 2D CAD + 17k-18k climate-zoned plants + photo imaging + custom quotes for $399.99/yr (half CanopyBid's $828/yr); PRO Landscape+ ($900/yr, just $72/yr more) bundles full 2D+3D+photo+AI + free iPad Companion; Rayon.design ($456/yr Solo / $984/yr 3-seat Studio) delivers browser 2D CAD + live object-bound takeoff/cost tables + Private Home Landscape templates; Sow Pro+ ($99.99/yr) delivers iPad/web 12k+ plants + live nursery pricing + auto plant schedules + branded proposals + client sign-off + AI renders; ArcSite ($99-$129/mo) delivers native iPad Apple Pencil 2D CAD + automated mulch/edging/planting takeoffs + on-site e-sign & payment collection; and gCADPlus ($95 one-time), Realtime Landscaping Architect ($599 one-time), Garden Planner ($48 one-time), Shoot Gardening (~£240/yr), and Morpholio Trace ($20-$50/yr) + PlantMaster ($250/yr with Vectorworks sync) lock down the budget and regional floors. CanopyBid Pro offers strictly fewer capabilities (no 3D, no photo imaging, no hardscapes, no e-sign/payments, no licensed cultivar photo DB) at 2x-8x the floor price.

enduring.justification: 0.5 (recurring annual workflow proven by DynaScape, PRO Landscape+, Vectorworks, PlantMaster, and ArcSite), strictly capped below 1.0 due to northern-climate winter pause/cancellation risk on monthly plans, zero downstream CRM/job-costing/payment lock-in by deliberate trade-off, and continuous feature encroachment from Sow Pro+ and Rayon.design.

killed.reason: BAD_IDEA — UNANIMOUS KILL (DO NOT BUILD). Live primary-source verification collapsed the deterministic ASB Problem Score 50x from 1.0 to 0.02 (10,000 Plausible x 0.5 Self-Aware x $1,000 Lucrative x 0.1 Liquid x 0.5 Eager-Identity x 0.1 Eager-Comparative x 0.5 Enduring / 625,000 = 0.02) — and down to 0.002 if narrowed to the $100-$300/yr solo Mac/iPad garden designer slice. Four independent fatal flaws kill the idea without rescue: (1) an airtight 'Less for More' competitor sandwich led by PRO Landscape Contractor standalone iPad ($399.99/yr), PRO Landscape+ ($900/yr with 2D+3D+photo+free iPad Companion), Rayon.design ($456/yr browser CAD + live takeoff tables), Sow Pro+ ($99.99/yr iPad/web 12k plants + live nursery pricing + proposals + sign-off), and ArcSite ($99-$129/mo iPad Apple Pencil CAD + takeoffs + e-sign/payments); (2) spreadsheet TAM arbitrage gluing unreachable non-English Europe onto two mutually contradictory personas; (3) an unlicensed botanical IP/photography wall (RHS & Monrovia closed); and (4) an unexecutable 3-in-1 solo engineering tarpit trapped inside a 12-week northern-climate winter switching window (Liquid = 0.1). Archive immediately to KILLED-IDEAS.md with zero code written.
